To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the effectiveness of sera in preventing the growth and metastasis of Moloney sarcoma and lymphomas correlated well with antibody titers measured in vitro by indirect membrane immunohistofluorescence and virus neutralization tests.

the effectiveness of sera in the protection of mice against transplantable Molony virus-induced tumors correlated with the antibody titers measured in the serum by indirect membrane immunolofluorescence and virus-neutralization tests.

the effectiveness of sera in protecting against transplantable Molony leukemia-induced tumors correlated closely with the serum antibody titers measured in three different tests, i.e., membrane immunofluoroscence, cytotoxicity and neutralization.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of antibody in the control of tumor growth.
the development of immunotherapies for the treatment of cancer.
the immunology of Moloney virus-induced tumors.

the sera from mice immunized against MSV-induced tumors, as measured by MF and neutralization, were effective in preventing tumor growth.
